findings.title: Removing --die-with-parent drops the only cleanup for abruptly-killed runners outside systemd
findings.detail: PR_SET_PDEATHSIG (what --die-with-parent sets) used to fire whenever the spawning thread's process exited for any reason, including an ungraceful crash or `kill -9` of the whole runner, not just the idle-Dispatch-thread case this change targets. The fix drops the flag unconditionally and relies entirely on systemd's default KillMode=control-group (Runner/oby-runner.service doesn't set it explicitly) to reap leftover bwrap/agent trees. That covers the documented systemd deployment, but Runner/README.md also documents running the binary directly for development/testing (`OBY_HOME=$(mktemp -d) … .build/release/oby-runner`), and RunnerTests itself spawns real bwrap sandboxes via the `bubblewrapRuns` tests. In those non-systemd contexts a hard crash or SIGKILL of the runner/test binary now leaves sandboxed child processes running indefinitely with nothing to reap them, where before this change they were (prematurely, which was the bug, but also incidentally on a real crash). No equivalent safety net (e.g. killing the bwrap process group, or re-adding die-with-parent while keeping the spawning thread alive) was added for the non-systemd paths.
